claims.text: Menu relies on soy sauce, dashi, and cured/pickled seafood; no gluten-free accommodation is documented, so cross-contamination should be assumed.
Soy-marinated dishes such as ikura shoyu-zuke are signature items, indicating standard (wheat-containing) soy sauce is used.
Set meals and small plates are seafood- and dashi-based; no vegan preparation is documented.

name: いも屋cafe 楽 (Imoya Cafe Tano)

claims.text: Desserts are made to order at the counter in front of you, so you can see the ingredients and speak directly with the owner-chef about what goes into each dish.

name: インドめし ティルパティ (Indomeshi Tirupati)

claims.text: The kitchen centers on a tandoor oven baking wheat-flour naan, so airborne flour and shared surfaces make cross-contact likely; no gluten-free handling is documented.

The vegetarian vegetable curry uses soy-meat dumplings and the menu relies heavily on dairy (naan, kulfi, likely cream/paneer dishes); no vegan-specific separation is documented, so confirm ghee/butter/milk per dish.
Offers a dedicated vegetable curry and vegetable set aimed at vegetarians, plus a choice of Koshihikari rice instead of naan.
Uses Himalayan rock salt and reduces oil for a lighter, more health-conscious style of Indian cooking.
Hojicha roasted tea, the shop's core offering, is naturally gluten-free and vegan.

name: 居酒屋割烹 源左ェ門 木倉町本店 (Izakaya Kappo Genzaemon Kiguramachi Honten)

claims.text: Cooking centers on regional Kaga dishes, sashimi with soy sauce, miso-grilled hoba miso, and dashi-based preparations, all typically using wheat-containing soy sauce and miso.
The menu is fish- and meat-forward (Kanazawa Port sashimi, nodoguro, Noto beef sukiyaki) with dashi used throughout, so vegetable dishes are not free of animal products.

name: ジャルダン ポール・ボキューズ (Jardin Paul Bocuse)

claims.text: Allergy consultations are accepted at the time of reservation.
A vegetarian menu is available with advance arrangement.

name: 地場料理と酒肴 季節会席 金澤 斉や (Jiba Ryori to Shuko Kisetsu Kaiseki Kanazawa)

claims.text: The signature jibuni uses wheat-flour-coated meat and Kanazawa fu (sudare-fu and nama-fu, which are wheat gluten), so wheat is central to the kitchen and shared prep is likely.
Seasoning is built on traditional Japanese soy sauce and dashi (including a white-soy eel glaze), which contain wheat; no wheat-free soy alternative is mentioned.
Dishes are dashi-, fish-, and meat-based throughout, so even vegetable items are not prepared vegan.

name: 加賀屋 金沢店 (Kagaya Kanazawa-ten)

claims.text: Kaga and kaiseki cuisine here relies heavily on wheat-based soy sauce and dashi; the menu also includes tempura and tonkatsu, so a shared kitchen handles wheat extensively.
The signature jibuni is simmered in a soy-sauce-and-dashi broth, and standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat.
Cuisine is built on bonito/kombu dashi and Japan Sea seafood; jibuni traditionally uses duck or chicken, so plant-only dining is not accommodated.
